chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, all from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Ya'qūb ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: In the son of Ādam there are three hundred and sixty veins; from these, one hundred and eighty are moving, and from these, one hundred and eighty are still. If the moving ones were to stay still, he would not sleep, and if the still ones were to move, he would not sleep.'

And it was so that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever it was morning, said: 'Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbil-'ālamīn' (The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds) frequently, upon every state, three hundred and sixty times, and whenever it was evening, said similar to that.'

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 360 veins and the morning/evening dhikr mentioned in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi links the Prophetic practice of reciting 'Al-Hamdu lillāhi rabbil-'ālamīn' 360 times to the traditional anatomical model of 360 veins, symbolizing a holistic balance of the body's faculties. In Shia scholarly tradition, this specific dhikr serves as a spiritual remedy that aligns the believer’s physical and spiritual states with divine praise, ensuring that every 'vein' or aspect of existence is engaged in gratitude.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said,

‘‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘In the son of Adam<sup>as</sup> there are three hundred and sixty veins – from these one hundred and eighty are moving and from these one hundred and eighty are still. If the moving ones were to stay still he would not (be able to) sleep, and if the still ones were to move, he would not (be able to) sleep; and it was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever it was morning, said:

‘الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ’ ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds, a lot, upon every state’, three hundred and sixty times, and whenever it was evening, said similar to that’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Humayd ibn Ziyad from al- Hassan ibn Muhammad all from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithami from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said that in a son of Adam there are three hundred sixty veins of which one hundred eighty are moving and one hundred eighty are quiet. If a moving vein becomes quiet one cannot sleep and if a quiet one moves one cannot sleep’.

The Messenger of Allah in the morning would say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, a great deal of praise in all conditions, three hundred sixty times and so also he would do in the evening.’”
